intro: Six messages about work. Some are ordinary jobs, so refusing everything is not the skill. Decide, then look.
reflection: Which message were you least sure of, and which way would the money have moved?

sources.title: Enforcement Directorate raids in a fake government job racket that sent fraudulent joining letters from email accounts imitating official ones (8 January 2026)

Ministry of Home Affairs: over 100 websites blocked for task-based part-time job frauds, in which a small commission is paid first and larger deposits are then frozen (Press Information Bureau, 6 December 2023)
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

sources.title: National Career Service: no fee is charged at any stage, and jobseekers should not pay fees to employers (accessed 22 September 2026)
sources.publisher: National Career Service, Ministry of Labour and Employment

screen.from: Office manager, the firm where you interviewed
lines: Your offer letter is ready to collect: stipend ₹12,000 a month.
Paid into your bank account on the 7th, from the firm's own account.
Bring your PAN card and bank details to the office on your joining day.

check.q: You had two interviews at their office last month, and the stipend matches what they said. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, and take your details to the office on the day
options.why: You met them, pay comes from their account to you, and your details go in person. Unsure? Call the number you already had.

options.text: Refuse, because it mentions your bank details
options.why: An employer needs your account to pay you. What matters is which way the money moves.

options.text: Accept, and reply now with your PAN and account number
options.why: The message asks for them in person. Sending them in a reply is what a fake offer is hoping for.

lines: Pay ₹1,000 to move to premium tasks.

check.q: The first ₹450 really reached your account. What do you do?

options.text: Pay the ₹1,000, since the ₹450 was real
options.why: The ₹450 was paid to win your trust. Once bigger deposits go in, they are frozen.

options.text: Pay once, and leave if the ₹3,000 does not come
options.why: Once paid, the ₹1,000 is gone either way. Deposits in these groups are frozen, not paid out.

options.text: Stop, pay nothing, and report the group
options.why: A job pays you. Paying to earn more is the sign, and the early ₹450 was the bait.

lines: Selected for data entry from home, ₹18,000 a month.
Pay ₹1,499 for your joining kit to start.

check.q: You applied to several data-entry adverts last week. What do you do?

options.text: Pay, since ₹1,499 is small next to ₹18,000 a month
options.why: The fee is what the message is for. A real employer pays you; it does not charge you to start.

options.text: Refuse: an employer pays you, never the other way round
options.why: A fee before any work, and no interview. The government's jobs portal tells jobseekers not to pay fees to employers.

options.text: Ask them to take the ₹1,499 from your first month's pay
options.why: You would still be paying to get a job. The fee is the point of the message, not the work.
